contents.html: Abstract
contents.html_ja: 要旨

contents.html: This document is part of a series intended to provide guidance to the Federal Government for using cryptography and NIST’s cryptographic standards to protect sensitive, but unclassified digitized information during transmission and while in storage. Special Publication (SP) 800-175A provides guidance on the determination of requirements for using cryptography. It includes a summary of laws and regulations concerning the protection of the Federal Government’s sensitive information, guidance regarding the conduct of risk assessments to determine what needs to be protected and how best to protect that information, and a discussion of the relevant security-related documents (e.g., various policy and practice documents).

contents.html: SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION
contents.html_ja: 第1節：はじめに

contents.html: 1.1 Background and Purpose
contents.html_ja: 1.1 背景および目的

contents.html: Cryptographic publications of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) provide guidance regarding how cryptographic protection is to be implemented, but do not specify when cryptographic protection is required. The decision regarding whether or not to employ cryptographic protection rests with the owner of the information to be protected. Decisions concerning the use of cryptographic protection are generally based on a thorough risk analysis that establishes the sensitivity of the information to be protected and the security controls that need to be used to protect that information, both during transmission and while in storage. This document provides guidance on the basis for determining requirements for using cryptography. It includes a summary of the laws, directives, standards, and guidelines concerning the protection of the Federal government’s sensitive but unclassified information; guidance regarding the conduct of risk assessments to determine what information needs to be protected and how best to protect that information; and a discussion of application-relevant security documentation (e.g., various policy and practice documents). While the use of this guideline outside the Federal Government is strictly voluntary, many of the processes and references included herein may be useful in non-federal contexts. The primary policy documents that apply to federal cryptographic systems include Public Laws, Presidential Executive Orders and Directives, and other guidance from Executive Office of the President organizations. Some Department of Commerce and NIST publications are identified in these policy documents as being mandatory for Federal organizations. Relevant NIST cryptographic publications are discussed in Special Publication (SP) 800-175B, Guideline for Using Cryptographic Standards in the Federal Government: Cryptographic Mechanisms.
contents.html_ja: 国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の暗号関連刊行物は、暗号保護の実装方法に関する指針を示すが、暗号保護がいつ必要となるかは規定しない。暗号保護を使用するかどうかは、保護対象情報の所有者が決定する。通常、その決定は、保護対象情報の機微性と、伝送中および保管中の情報を保護するために必要なセキュリティ管理策を明らかにする徹底したリスク分析に基づく。本書は、暗号技術を使用する要件を決定する基礎について指針を示す。連邦政府の機微な非機密情報を保護する法律、指令、標準および指針の概要、保護対象情報と最適な保護方法を決定するリスク評価の実施指針、ならびにアプリケーションに関連するセキュリティ文書（各種方針および実務文書など）の説明を含む。本指針を連邦政府外で使用することは完全に任意だが、記載された多くのプロセスおよび参考文献は非連邦環境でも有用な場合がある。連邦暗号システムに適用される主な方針文書には、公法、大統領令および大統領指令、大統領府機関からのその他の指針がある。商務省およびNISTの刊行物の一部は、これらの方針文書により連邦組織に義務付けられている。本書に関連するNIST暗号刊行物は、SP 800-175B「連邦政府における暗号規格の使用に関する指針：暗号メカニズム」で説明されている。

contents.html: Authentication
contents.html_ja: 認証

contents.html: As used in this document, a process that provides assurance of the source and integrity of information that is communicated or stored, or that provides assurance of an entity’s identity.
contents.html_ja: 本書でいう認証とは、通信または保管される情報の送信元および完全性を保証するプロセス、またはエンティティの識別情報を保証するプロセスである。

contents.html: Authorization
contents.html_ja: 認可

contents.html: The official management decision given by a senior organizational official to authorize the operation of an information system and to explicitly accept the risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of security controls.
contents.html_ja: 情報システムの運用を認可し、合意済みのセキュリティ管理策の実装に基づいて、組織の運用および資産、個人、他組織ならびに国に対するリスクを明示的に受け入れる、上級組織職員による正式な管理上の決定。

contents.html: Breach
contents.html_ja: 侵害

contents.html: The loss of control, compromise, unauthorized disclosure, unauthorized acquisition, unauthorized access, or any similar term referring to situations where persons other than authorized users, or where authorized users take actions for an other than authorized purposes, have access or potential access to sensitive information, whether physical or electronic.
contents.html_ja: 制御の喪失、侵害、不正開示、不正取得、不正アクセス、または類似の状況を指す用語。すなわち、認可された利用者以外の者が機微情報にアクセスする状況、または認可された利用者が認可されていない目的で行動し、物理的または電子的な機微情報にアクセスする、もしくはアクセスできる可能性がある状況。

contents.html: Categorization
contents.html_ja: 分類

contents.html: The process of determining the security category for information or an information system. Security categorization methodologies are described in CNSS Instruction 1253 for national security systems and in FIPS Publication 199 for other than national security systems.
contents.html_ja: 情報または情報システムのセキュリティカテゴリを決定するプロセス。国家安全保障システムにはCNSS指令1253、その他のシステムにはFIPS刊行物199で分類方法が説明されている。

contents.html: Ciphertext
contents.html_ja: 暗号文

contents.html: Data in its encrypted form.
contents.html_ja: 暗号化された形式のデータ。

contents.html: Confidentiality
contents.html_ja: 機密性

contents.html: The property that sensitive information is not disclosed to unauthorized entities.

contents.html: 2.1 E-Government Act of 2002 (FISMA)
contents.html_ja: 2.1 2002年電子政府法（FISMA）

contents.html: Title III of Public Law 107-347 is cited as the Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002 (FISMA) and has been incorporated into Sections 20 and 21 of the NIST Act. Paragraph 3543 of the Act provides for the Executive Office of the President to coordinate the development of standards and guidelines by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) (under Section 20 of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act [15 U.S.C. 278g–3]) with agencies and offices operating or exercising control of national security systems (including the National Security Agency) to assure, to the maximum extent feasible, that such standards and guidelines are complementary with standards and guidelines developed for national security systems. Section 302 of the Act directs the Secretary of Commerce (under Section 11331 of Title 40 United States Code (U.S.C.)) to prescribe standards and guidelines pertaining to federal information systems, based on standards and guidelines developed by NIST. Section 302 of the Act makes these standards compulsory and binding to the extent determined necessary by the Secretary to improve the efficiency of the operation or security of federal information systems, and also states that the standards shall include information security standards that— (1) Provide minimum information security requirements as determined under Section 20(b) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act (15 U.S.C. 278g–3(b)); and (2) Are otherwise necessary to improve the security of federal information and information systems.
contents.html_ja: 公法107-347の第III編は、2002年連邦情報セキュリティマネジメント法（FISMA）として引用され、NIST法第20条および第21条に組み込まれている。同法第3543項は、米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）による規格・指針の策定（NIST法第20条[15 U.S.C. 278g–3]に基づく）を、国家安全保障システムを運用または管理する機関・事務所（国家安全保障局を含む）と調整し、実行可能な最大限の範囲で、それらの規格・指針が国家安全保障システム向けに策定された規格・指針と補完的なものとなるようにすることを、大統領府の役割として定める。同法第302条は、商務長官に対し、（合衆国法典（U.S.C.）第40編第11331条に基づき）NISTが策定した規格・指針に基づいて、連邦情報システムに関する規格・指針を規定するよう指示する。同法第302条は、連邦情報システムの運用効率またはセキュリティを向上させるために必要と商務長官が判断する範囲で、これらの規格を強制的かつ拘束力のあるものとし、また、規格には次の情報セキュリティ規格を含めなければならないと定める— (1) NIST法第20条(b)（15 U.S.C. 278g–3(b)）に基づき定められる情報セキュリティの最低要件を定めるもの; および (2) その他、連邦の情報および情報システムのセキュリティを向上させるために必要なもの。

contents.html: Only the President is assigned the authority to disapprove or modify these standards. The heads of executive agencies may employ standards for the cost-effective information security of information systems within or under the supervision of that agency that are more stringent than the standards prescribed by the Secretary of Commerce if the more stringent standards — (1) contain at least the applicable standards made compulsory and binding by the Secretary; and (2) are otherwise consistent with policies and guidelines issued under Section 3543 of Title 44 U.S.C. contents.html: The Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health (HITECH) Act of 2009 is an example of sector-specific legislation that provides for the encryption of information using NIST standards. The HITECH Act was enacted, as Title XIII of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009, to promote the adoption and meaningful use of health information technology. Subtitle D of the HITECH Act addresses the privacy and security concerns associated with the electronic transmission of health information, in part, through several provisions that strengthen the civil and criminal enforcement of the rules enacted by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) of 19961. The HITECH Act mandates the notification of a breach of unsecured protected health information (PHI), but provided that breaches do not have to be reported if the data involved is rendered unreadable via encryption2.

contents.html: The Cybersecurity Enhancement Act of 2014 extends NIST’s security standards activity to include direct support to the private sector. This extension is significant in that it specifically authorizes cybersecurity support for organizations outside the U.S. Federal government. contents.html: HSPD-7 establishes a national policy for federal departments and agencies to identify and prioritize United States critical infrastructure and key resources and to protect them from terrorist attacks. The Directive directs the Department of Commerce, in coordination with the Department for Homeland Security, to work with the private sector, research, academic, and government organizations to improve technology for cyber systems and promote other critical infrastructure efforts, including using its authority under the Defense Production Act3 to assure the timely availability of industrial products, materials, and services to meet homeland security requirements.

contents.html: 3.2 HSPD-12: Policies for a Common Identification Standard for Federal

contents.html: This directive mandates the development of a federal standard for secure and reliable forms of identification. HSPD-12 directs the Secretary of Commerce to promulgate, in accordance with applicable laws, a federal standard for secure and reliable forms of identification in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, the Attorney General, the Secretary of Homeland Security, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), and the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy. The Secretary of Commerce is directed to periodically review the Standard and update the Standard, as appropriate, in consultation with the affected agencies. For purposes of this directive, "Secure and reliable forms of identification" means identification that: (a) Is issued, based on sound criteria for verifying an individual employee's identity; (b) Is strongly resistant to identity fraud, tampering, counterfeiting, and terrorist exploitation; (c) Can be rapidly authenticated electronically; and (d) Is issued only by providers whose reliability has been established by an official accreditation process. The Standard to be developed is directed to include graduated criteria, from least secure to most secure, to ensure flexibility in selecting the appropriate level of security for each application.
contents.html_ja: この指令は、安全で信頼性の高い身分証明方式に関する連邦標準の策定を義務付ける。HSPD-12は商務長官に対し、国務長官、国防長官、司法長官、国土安全保障長官、行政管理予算局（OMB）局長および科学技術政策局長と協議の上、適用法に従って、安全で信頼性の高い身分証明方式に関する連邦標準を公布するよう指示する。商務長官は、影響を受ける機関と協議の上、定期的に標準を見直し、適宜更新するよう指示されている。この指令において「安全で信頼性の高い身分証明方式」とは、次の身分証明を意味する: (a) 職員個人の身元を検証するための適切な基準に基づいて発行される; (b) なりすまし、改ざん、偽造およびテロリストによる悪用に対して強い耐性がある; (c) 電子的に迅速に認証できる; および (d) 公式な認定プロセスによって信頼性が確立された提供者のみが発行する。策定する標準には、各アプリケーションに適切なセキュリティレベルを柔軟に選択できるよう、最も安全性の低いものから最も高いものまで段階的な基準を含めるよう指示されている。

contents.html: Office of Management and Budget Circular A-1304 establishes general policy for the planning, budgeting, governance, acquisition, and management of Federal information, personnel, equipment, funds, IT resources and supporting infrastructure and services. The appendices to this Circular also include responsibilities for protecting Federal information resources and managing personally identifiable information (PII). The requirements of this Circular apply to the information resources management activities of all agencies of the Executive Branch of the Federal Government. The requirements of Circular A-130 apply to management activities concerning all information resources in any medium (unless otherwise noted), including paper and electronic information. When an agency acts as a service provider, the ultimate responsibility for compliance with applicable requirements of this Circular is not shifted (to the service provider). Agencies are required to describe the responsibilities of service providers in relevant agreements with the service providers. Agencies are not required to apply this Circular to national security systems (defined in 44 U.S.C. § 35525), but are encouraged to do so where appropriate. For national security systems, agencies shall follow applicable statutes, executive orders, directives, and internal agency policies. Unlike most other cybersecurity-related directives and mandates, Circular A-130 does impose specific requirements for encryption and digital signatures. The following material identifies particularly salient requirements associated with cryptography and the underlying risk management determinations. contents.html: m. Encryption

contents.html: When the assessed risk indicates the need, agencies must encrypt Federal information at rest and in transit unless otherwise protected by alternative physical and logical safeguards implemented at multiple layers, including networks, systems, applications, and data. Encrypting information at rest and in transit helps to protect the confidentiality and integrity of such information by making it less susceptible to unauthorized disclosure or modification. Agencies must apply encryption requirements to Federal information categorized as either moderate or high impact in accordance with FIPS Publication 199 unless encrypting such information is technically unfeasible or would demonstrably affect their ability to carry out their respective mission, functions, or operations. In situations where the use of encryption is technically infeasible, for example, due to an aging legacy system, agencies must initiate the appropriate system or system component upgrade or replacement actions at the earliest opportunity to be able to accommodate such safeguarding technologies. Authorizing officials who choose to operate information systems without the use of required encryption technologies must carefully assess the risk in doing so, and they must receive written approval for the exception from the agency CIO, in consultation with the SAOP (as appropriate). Only FIPS-validated cryptography is approved for use in Federal information systems covered by this policy.

contents.html: n. Digital Signatures

contents.html: Digital signatures can mitigate a variety of security vulnerabilities by providing authentication and non-repudiation capabilities, and ensuring the integrity of Federal information whether such information is used in day-to-day operations or archived for future use. Additionally, digital signatures can help agencies streamline mission or business processes and transition manual processes to more automated processes to include, for example, online transactions. Because of the advantages provided by this technology, OMB expects agencies to implement digital signature capabilities in accordance with Federal PKI policy, and NIST standards and guidelines. For employees and contractors, agencies must require the use of the digital signature capability of Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials. For individuals that fall outside the scope of PIV applicability, agencies should leverage approved Federal PKI credentials when using digital signatures.
contents.html_ja: デジタル署名は、認証および否認防止機能を提供し、日常業務で使用する場合も将来利用のためにアーカイブする場合も連邦情報の完全性を確保することで、さまざまなセキュリティ脆弱性を緩和できる。さらに、デジタル署名は機関の任務・業務プロセスの合理化や、オンライン取引などを含む手動プロセスの自動化移行を支援できる。この技術の利点から、OMBは機関に対し、連邦PKI方針およびNIST標準・ガイドラインに従ってデジタル署名機能を実装することを期待する。職員および請負業者には、個人識別検証（PIV）認証情報のデジタル署名機能の使用を義務付けなければならない。PIVの適用範囲外の個人がデジタル署名を使用する場合、機関は承認済みの連邦PKI認証情報を活用すべきである。

contents.html: OMB Memorandum M-06-16 notes that NIST provided a checklist for the protection of remote information. The intent of implementing the checklist is to compensate for the lack of physical security controls when information is removed from, or accessed from outside the agency location. In addition to using the NIST checklist, OMB M-06-16 recommended that all departments and agencies encrypt all data on mobile computers/devices that carry agency data unless the data is determined to be non-sensitive, in writing, by a Deputy Secretary or an individual that he/she may designate in writing; and allow remote access only with two-factor authentication where one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the computer gaining access.
contents.html_ja: OMB覚書M-06-16は、NISTが遠隔地にある情報を保護するためのチェックリストを提供したと述べている。このチェックリストの実施は、情報を機関の施設外へ持ち出す場合、または施設外からアクセスする場合に、物理的セキュリティ管理策の不足を補うことを目的とする。NISTチェックリストの利用に加え、OMB M-06-16は、機関データを保持するモバイルコンピュータ／デバイス上のすべてのデータを暗号化することを各省庁・機関に推奨した。ただし、副長官または副長官が書面で指名した者が書面で非機微情報と判断した場合を除く。また、遠隔アクセスは二要素認証を用いる場合に限り許可し、要素の一つはアクセス元コンピュータとは別のデバイスから提供することを推奨した。

contents.html: Implementation of HSPD-12

contents.html: OMB Memorandum M-06-18 provides updated direction for the acquisition of products and services for the implementation of Homeland Security Presidential Directive-12 (HSPD-12), Policy for a Common Identification Standard for Federal Employees and Contractors, and also provides the status of implementation efforts. HSPD-12 notes that both NIST and the General Services Administration (GSA) have established evaluation programs for the testing and evaluation of specific products and services needed for the implementation of HSPD-12, and that NIST has established the NIST Personal Identity Verification Program (NPIVP) to test and validate Personal Identity Verification (PIV) components and sub-systems required by Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201. At the time that the Memorandum was signed, an NPIVP validation program provided for the testing and validation of PIV card applications and PIV middleware for conformance to FIPS 201 and the interface specifications of NIST SP 800-73, Interfaces for Personal Identity Verification. NIST was also noted as having published derived test requirements as NIST SP 800-85A, PIV Card Application and Middleware Test Guidelines. All of the tests under NPIVP are handled by third-party test laboratories that are now designated as interim NPIVP Test Facilities. FIPS 140-2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules23, requires the testing and validation of the cryptographic modules of PIV cards and other products performing cryptographic functions. This testing is performed by the accredited third-party facilities designated to perform NPIVP testing.

contents.html: 3.8 OMB Memorandum M-07-16, Safeguarding Against and Responding to the
Breach of Personally Identifiable Information
contents.html_ja: 個人識別情報の侵害に対する保護および対応

contents.html: OMB Memorandum M-07-16 requires agencies to develop and implement a breach24 notification policy within 120 days from the OMB Memorandum’s having been signed. The Memorandum specifically recommends using encryption, strong authentication procedures, and other security controls to make information unusable by unauthorized individuals. The attachments to this memorandum outline the framework within which agencies must develop this breach notification policy, while ensuring that proper safeguards are in place to protect the information. Elements of the framework include requirements to: a. Assign an impact level to all information and information systems. Agencies must follow the processes outlined in FIPS 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems, to categorize all information and information systems according to the standard’s three levels of impact (i.e., low, moderate, and high). Agencies should generally consider categorizing sensitive, personally identifiable information (and information systems within which such information resides) as moderate or high impact. b. Implement minimum security requirements and controls. For each of the impact levels identified above, agencies must implement the minimum security requirements and minimum (baseline) security controls set forth in FIPS 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems, and NIST Special Publication 800-53, Recommended Security Controls for Federal Information Systems25, respectively. c. Certify and accredit information systems. Agencies must certify and accredit (C&A) all information systems supporting the operations and assets of the agency, including those provided or managed by another agency, contractor, or other source. The specific procedures for conducting C&A are set out in NIST Special Publication 800-37, Guide for the Security Certification and Accreditation of Federal Information Systems,26 and include guidance for the continuous monitoring of certain security controls. Agencies’ continuous monitoring should assess a subset of the management, operational, and technical controls used to safeguard such information (e.g., Privacy Impact Assessments). The Memorandum’s requirements include 1) encryption using only NIST-certified cryptographic modules27 for all data on mobile computers/devices carrying agency data, unless the data is determined to not be sensitive, in writing, by a Deputy Secretary28 or a senior-level individual he/she may designate in writing; and 2) allowing remote access only with two-factor authentication where one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the computer gaining access.
contents.html_ja: OMB覚書M-07-16は、覚書署名から120日以内に、機関が漏えい24通知方針を策定し実施することを求める。この覚書は、権限のない者が情報を利用できないようにするため、暗号化、強固な認証手順、その他のセキュリティ管理策を用いることを特に推奨している。添付文書は、情報を保護するための適切な安全策を確保しつつ、機関が漏えい通知方針を策定する際の枠組みを示す。枠組みには次の要件が含まれる。a. すべての情報および情報システムに影響度を割り当てる。機関はFIPS 199「連邦情報および情報システムのセキュリティ分類規格」に示された手順に従い、同規格の3段階（低、中、高）に基づいてすべての情報および情報システムを分類する。機関は一般に、機微な個人識別情報とその情報を保存する情報システムを中または高の影響度に分類することを検討すべきである。b. 最低限のセキュリティ要件と管理策を実装する。上記の各影響度について、機関はFIPS 200「連邦情報および情報システムの最低限のセキュリティ要件」とNIST特別刊行物800-53「連邦情報システムの推奨セキュリティ管理策」25にそれぞれ定められた最低限のセキュリティ要件および最低限（ベースライン）のセキュリティ管理策を実装する。c. 情報システムを認証し、認定する。機関は、他機関、請負業者、その他の供給元が提供または管理するものを含め、機関の業務および資産を支援するすべての情報システムを認証・認定（C&A）する。C&Aを実施する具体的な手順は、NIST特別刊行物800-37「連邦情報システムのセキュリティ認証および認定ガイド」26に示され、一部のセキュリティ管理策の継続的監視に関する指針も含む。機関の継続的監視では、当該情報を保護するために用いる管理的・運用的・技術的管理策の一部（例：プライバシー影響評価）を評価すべきである。覚書はさらに、機関データを保持するモバイルコンピュータ／デバイス上のすべてのデータについて、NIST認証済み暗号モジュール27のみを用いた暗号化を求める。ただし、副長官28または副長官が書面で指名した上級職員が書面で非機微情報と判断した場合を除く。また、遠隔アクセスは二要素認証を用いる場合に限り許可し、要素の一つはアクセス元コンピュータとは別のデバイスから提供する。

contents.html: OMB Memorandum M-08-23 required the Federal Government to deploy Domain Name System Security Extensions (DNSSEC) to the top-level .gov domain by January 2009. The top-level .gov domain includes the registrar, registry, and DNS server operations. This policy requires that the top-level .gov domain will be DNSSEC-signed, and processes to enable secure delegated sub-domains will be developed. Signing the top-level .gov domain is a critical procedure necessary for broad deployment of DNSSEC, increases the utility of DNSSEC, and simplifies lower-level deployment by agencies. The Memorandum also required agencies to develop plans of action and milestones for the deployment of DNSSEC to all applicable information systems. Appropriate DNSSEC capabilities were required to be deployed and operational by December 2009. The plans were to follow recommendations in NIST SP 800-81, Secure Domain Name System (DNS) Deployment Guide, and address the particular requirements described in NIST SP 800-53r129, Recommended Security Controls for Federal Information Systems. The plans were also to report agencies’ current levels of compliance with the current DNSSEC requirements of NIST SP 800-53r1, and document plans of action and milestones that assume the scope of the requirement to operate DNSSEC signed zones. SP 800-53’s control SC-20 was required to be expanded to cover all FISMA information systems (including low-impact systems) in its revision 3. The plans were to ensure that all agency .gov domains were DNSSEC-signed by December 2009.

contents.html: Because these guidelines are jointly issued, DOD and ODNI policies for national security systems should incorporate these guidelines. Is use of National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) publications required? Yes. For non-national security programs and information systems, agencies must follow NIST standards and guidelines unless otherwise stated by OMB. For legacy information systems, agencies are expected to be in compliance with NIST standards and guidelines within one year of the publication date unless otherwise directed by OMB. The one-year compliance date for revisions to NIST publications applies only to the new and/or updated material in the publications. For information systems under development or for legacy systems undergoing significant changes, agencies are expected to be in compliance with the NIST publications immediately upon deployment of the information system. Are NIST guidelines flexible? Yes. While agencies are required to follow NIST standards and guidelines in accordance with OMB policy, there is flexibility within NIST's guidelines (specifically in the 800-series) in how agencies apply them. However, NIST Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) publications are mandatory. Unless specified by additional implementing policy by OMB, NIST guidelines generally allow agencies latitude in their application. Consequently, the application of NIST guidelines by agencies can result in different security solutions that are equally acceptable and compliant with the guidelines. FISMA, OMB policy, and NIST standards and guidelines require agency security programs to be risk-based. Who is responsible for deciding the acceptable level of risk (e.g., the CIO, program officials and system owners, or the IG)? Are the IGs’ independent evaluations also to be risk-based? What if they disagree? The agency head ultimately is responsible for deciding the acceptable level of risk for their agency. System owners, program officials, and CIOs provide input for this decision. Such decisions must reflect policies from OMB and standards and guidelines from NIST (particularly FIPS 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems, and FIPS 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Security, as well as SP 800-39, Managing Information Security Risk). An information system' s Authorizing Official takes responsibility for accepting any residual risk, thus they are held accountable for managing the security for that system. IG evaluations are intended to independently assess that the agency is applying a risk-based approach to their information security programs and the information systems that support the conduct of agency missions and business functions. For example, when reviewing the assessment in support of an individual security authorization, the IG would generally assess whether: 1) the assessment was performed in the manner prescribed in NIST guidelines and agency policy, 2) controls are being implemented as stated in any planning documentation, and 3) continuous monitoring is adequate given the system impact level of the system and information. Are there security requirements specific for mobile devices (e.g. smartphones and tablets)? All existing Federal requirements for data protection and remote access are applicable to mobile devices. For example, the security requirements in OMB Circular A-130, FIPS 140-2, Security Requirements for Cryptographic Modules, FIPS 199, Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems, and FIPS 200, Minimum Security Requirements for Federal Information and Information Systems, apply (including appropriate security controls specified in SP 800-53). Agencies should specify security requirements during the acquisition process and ensure that procurements capture the requirements of the Federal Acquisition Regulation31 (e.g., 52.225-5, Trade Agreements), OMB policy (e.g., M-06-16 and M-07-16), and NIST standards and guidelines. Additional guidance regarding the use and management of mobile devices will be developed, as appropriate.
contents.html_ja: これらのガイドラインは共同発行されているため、国家安全保障システムに関するDODおよびODNIの方針には、これらのガイドラインを取り入れるべきである。国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の刊行物の使用は必須か。回答：国家安全保障以外のプログラムおよび情報システムについて、OMBが別途定めない限り、機関はNIST標準およびガイドラインに従わなければならない。レガシー情報システムについては、OMBから別途指示がない限り、刊行日から1年以内にNIST標準およびガイドラインへ準拠することが期待される。NIST刊行物の改訂に対する1年間の準拠期限は、新規または更新された内容にのみ適用される。開発中の情報システム、または大幅な変更を受けるレガシーシステムについては、導入時点でNIST刊行物に準拠することが期待される。NISTガイドラインには柔軟性があるか。回答：ある。OMB方針に従い機関はNIST標準およびガイドラインに従う必要がある一方で、NISTガイドライン（特に800シリーズ）の適用方法には柔軟性がある。ただし、NIST連邦情報処理標準（FIPS）の刊行物は必須である。OMBが追加の実施方針を定めていない限り、NISTガイドラインは一般に適用方法について機関に裁量を認める。そのため、機関がNISTガイドラインを適用した結果、同等に受け入れ可能でガイドラインに適合する異なるセキュリティ対策が採用されることがある。FISMA、OMB方針、NIST標準およびガイドラインは、機関のセキュリティプログラムをリスクベースとすることを求める。許容可能なリスク水準（例：CIO、プログラム担当者、システム所有者、監察総監（IG）のいずれが決定するか）を決める責任は誰にあるか。IGによる独立評価もリスクベースであるべきか。意見が一致しない場合はどうするか。最終的に、機関にとって許容可能なリスク水準を決定する責任は機関の長にある。システム所有者、プログラム担当者、CIOはこの判断に意見を提供する。判断にはOMB方針とNIST標準・ガイドライン（特にFIPS 199「連邦情報および情報システムのセキュリティ分類規格」、FIPS 200「連邦情報および情報システムの最低限のセキュリティ要件」、ならびにSP 800-39「情報セキュリティリスクの管理」）を反映しなければならない。情報システムの認可担当官は残留リスクを受容する責任を負い、そのシステムのセキュリティ管理について説明責任を負う。IGの評価は、機関が情報セキュリティプログラムおよび機関の任務・業務機能を支える情報システムに対してリスクベースのアプローチを採用しているかを独立して評価することを目的とする。例えば、個別のセキュリティ認可を裏付ける評価を審査する場合、IGは通常、1) NISTガイドラインおよび機関方針に定める方法で評価が実施されたか、2) 計画文書に記載されたとおりに管理策が実装されているか、3) システムと情報の影響度に照らして継続的監視が十分か、を評価する。スマートフォンやタブレットなどのモバイルデバイスに固有のセキュリティ要件はあるか。連邦政府の既存のデータ保護および遠隔アクセス要件は、すべてモバイルデバイスにも適用される。例えば、OMB通達A-130、FIPS 140-2「暗号モジュールのセキュリティ要件」、FIPS 199「連邦情報および情報システムのセキュリティ分類規格」、FIPS 200「連邦情報および情報システムの最低限のセキュリティ要件」の要件（SP 800-53で規定される適切なセキュリティ管理策を含む）が適用される。機関は調達時にセキュリティ要件を明示し、調達契約に連邦調達規則31（例：52.225-5「貿易協定」）、OMB方針（例：M-06-16およびM-07-16）、NIST標準およびガイドラインの要件を盛り込むべきである。モバイルデバイスの使用および管理に関する追加ガイダンスは、必要に応じて策定される予定である。

contents.html: 4.1 Information Management Policy
contents.html_ja: 4.1 情報管理方針

contents.html: An organization’s Information Management Policy specifies what information is to be collected or created, and how it is to be managed. An organization’s management establishes this policy using industry standards of good practices, legal requirements regarding the organization’s information, and organizational goals that must be achieved using the information that the organization will be collecting and creating. An Information Management Policy typically identifies management roles and responsibilities and establishes the authorization required for people performing these information-management duties. It also specifies what information is to be considered sensitive and how it is to be protected. In particular, this policy specifies what categories of information need to be protected against unauthorized disclosure, modification or destruction. These specifications form the foundation for an Information Security Policy and dictate the levels of confidentiality, integrity, availability, and source-authentication protections that must be provided for differing categories of sensitive information (see SP 800-130, A Framework for Designing Cryptographic Key Management Systems). Section 4.1 of SP 800-152, A Profile for U.S. Federal Cryptographic Key Management Systems, provides requirements for the content of an Information Management Policy for federal agencies.
contents.html_ja: 組織の情報管理方針は、収集または作成する情報とその管理方法を定める。組織の経営層は、適正な業務慣行に関する業界標準、組織の情報に関する法的要件、および収集・作成する情報を用いて達成する組織目標に基づいて方針を策定する。情報管理方針では通常、管理上の役割と責任を定め、情報管理業務を行う者に必要な権限を規定する。また、機微情報と見なす情報、およびその保護方法も定める。特に、この方針は、不正開示、改変、破壊から保護すべき情報カテゴリを指定する。これらの指定は情報セキュリティ方針の基礎となり、機微情報のカテゴリごとに必要な機密性、完全性、可用性、送信元認証の保護水準を決定する（SP 800-130「暗号鍵管理システム設計の枠組み」参照）。SP 800-152「米国連邦暗号鍵管理システムのプロファイル」4.1節には、連邦機関の情報管理方針に含める内容の要件が示されている。

contents.html: 4.2 Information Security Policy
contents.html_ja: 4.2 情報セキュリティ方針

contents.html: An organization’s Information Security Policy is created to support and enforce portions of the organization’s Information Management Policy by specifying in more detail what information is to be protected from anticipated threats and how that protection is to be attained. The rules for collecting, protecting, and distributing sensitive information in both paper and electronic form are specified in this policy. The inputs to the Information Security Policy include, but are not limited to, the Information Management Policy specifications, the potential threats to the security of the organization’s information, and the risks involved with the unauthorized disclosure, modification, and destruction or loss of the information. The outputs of the Information Security Policy include the information sensitivity levels (e.g., low, medium, or high) assigned to various categories of information and the high-level rules for protecting the information (see SP 800-130, A Framework for Designing Cryptographic Key Management Systems). Section 4.2 of SP 800-152 provides requirements for the content of an Information Security Policy for federal agencies.
contents.html_ja: 組織の情報セキュリティ方針は、予想される脅威から保護すべき情報と保護方法をより詳しく定め、情報管理方針の一部を支援・実施するために策定される。この方針は、紙媒体と電子媒体の機微情報を収集、保護、配布するための規則を定める。入力となる情報には、情報管理方針の仕様、組織の情報セキュリティに対する潜在的脅威、情報の不正開示・改変・破壊・喪失に伴うリスクなどが含まれるが、これらに限定されない。方針の出力には、さまざまな情報カテゴリに割り当てる機微度（低、中、高など）と、情報を保護するための高水準の規則が含まれる（SP 800-130「暗号鍵管理システム設計の枠組み」参照）。SP 800-152の4.2節には、連邦機関の情報セキュリティ方針に含める内容の要件が示されている。

contents.html: 4.3 Key Management Policies
contents.html_ja: 4.3 鍵管理方針

contents.html: Each organization that manages cryptographic systems that are intended to protect sensitive information should base the management of the keys used in those systems on an organizational policy statement. The Key Management Policy includes descriptions of the authorization and protection objectives and constraints that apply to the generation, distribution, accounting, storage, use, recovery and destruction of cryptographic keying material, and the cryptographic services to be provided (e.g., message authentication, digital signature, and encryption). Further information and requirements for Key Management Policies is provided in Section 3 of SP 800-57 Part 2, Recommendation for Key Management, Part 2: Best Practices for Key Management Organization. Key-Management Systems manage the cryptographic keys used to protect an organization’s sensitive information. Federal organizations may operate their own key-management systems, or may contract for key-management services. Information and requirements on the key management systems that manage cryptographic keys is provided in SP 800-152.
contents.html_ja: 機微情報を保護する暗号システムを管理する各組織は、それらのシステムで使用する鍵の管理を組織の方針に基づいて行うべきである。鍵管理方針には、暗号鍵素材の生成、配布、記録管理、保管、使用、復旧、破棄、および提供する暗号サービス（メッセージ認証、デジタル署名、暗号化など）に適用される権限付与・保護の目的と制約を記述する。鍵管理方針の詳細および要件は、SP 800-57第2部「鍵管理に関する勧告、第2部：鍵管理組織のベストプラクティス」第3節に示されている。鍵管理システムは、組織の機微情報を保護するために使う暗号鍵を管理する。連邦組織は、自組織で鍵管理システムを運用することも、鍵管理サービスを委託することもできる。暗号鍵を管理する鍵管理システムに関する情報と要件はSP 800-152に示されている。

contents.html: SECTION 5: RISK MANAGEMENT PROCESS
contents.html_ja: 第5節：リスク管理プロセス

contents.html: SP 800-37, Guide for Applying the Risk Management Framework to Federal Information Systems: A Security Lifecycle Approach, provides guidelines for applying the Risk Management Framework to federal information systems to include conducting the activities of security categorization,33 security control selection and implementation, security control assessment, information system authorization,34 and security control monitoring. The guidelines have been developed:
contents.html_ja: SP 800-37「連邦情報システムへのリスク管理フレームワーク適用ガイド：セキュリティライフサイクルアプローチ」は、セキュリティ分類33、セキュリティ管理策の選択と実装、セキュリティ管理策の評価、情報システムの認可34、セキュリティ管理策の監視など、連邦情報システムにリスク管理フレームワークを適用するためのガイドラインを示す。このガイドラインは次を目的として策定された。

contents.html: To ensure that managing information-system-related security risks is consistent with the organization’s mission/business objectives and overall risk strategy established by the senior leadership through the risk executive (function);
contents.html_ja: 情報システムに関連するセキュリティリスクの管理を、組織の任務・業務目標およびリスク担当役員（機能）を通じて上級幹部が定めた全体的なリスク戦略と整合させる。

contents.html: To ensure that information security requirements, including the necessary security controls, are integrated into the organization’s enterprise architecture and system development life cycle processes;
contents.html_ja: 必要なセキュリティ管理策を含む情報セキュリティ要件を、組織のエンタープライズアーキテクチャおよびシステム開発ライフサイクルプロセスに組み込む。

contents.html: To support consistent, well-informed, and ongoing security authorization decisions (through continuous monitoring), transparency of security and risk management-related information, and reciprocity;35 and
contents.html_ja: 継続的監視を通じ、一貫性があり十分な情報に基づく継続的なセキュリティ認可の判断、セキュリティおよびリスク管理情報の透明性、ならびに相互承認を支援する。35 また、

contents.html: To achieve more secure information and information systems within the federal government through the implementation of appropriate risk mitigation strategies.
contents.html_ja: 適切なリスク軽減戦略を実施し、連邦政府内の情報および情報システムのセキュリティを高める。

contents.html: When dealing with cryptographic functions, the tasks involved in applying the Risk Management Framework to information systems focus more on:
contents.html_ja: 暗号機能を扱う場合、情報システムにリスク管理フレームワークを適用する作業では、次の点をより重視する。

contents.html: The categorization of information and information systems and the selection of security controls than on the implementation of security controls,
contents.html_ja: 情報および情報システムの分類とセキュリティ管理策の選択に対して、セキュリティ管理策の実装に対してよりも、

contents.html: The assessment of security control effectiveness,
contents.html_ja: セキュリティ管理策の有効性の評価、

contents.html: The authorization of the information system, and
contents.html_ja: 情報システムの認可、および

contents.html: The ongoing monitoring of security controls and the security state of the information system.
contents.html_ja: セキュリティ管理策および情報システムのセキュリティ状態の継続的な監視。

contents.html: 33 FIPS 199 provides security-categorization guidance for non-national security systems. CNSS Instruction 1253 provides similar guidance for national security systems.
contents.html_ja: 33 FIPS 199は、国家安全保障以外のシステムに対するセキュリティ分類の指針を示す。国家安全保障システムについては、CNSS指示1253が同様の指針を示す。

contents.html: 34 System authorization is the official management decision given by a senior organizational official to authorize the operation of an information system and to explicitly accept the risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of security controls.
contents.html_ja: 34 システム認可とは、合意された一連のセキュリティ管理策が実装されていることを根拠に、情報システムの運用を許可し、組織の業務・資産、個人、他の組織、国家に対するリスクを明示的に受容する、組織の上級幹部による正式な管理上の決定である。

contents.html: 35 Reciprocity is the mutual agreement among participating organizations to accept each other’s security assessments in order to reuse information-system resources and/or to accept each other’s assessed security posture in order to share information. Reciprocity is best achieved by promoting the concept of transparency (i.e., making sufficient evidence regarding the security state of an information system available, so that an authorizing official from another organization can use that evidence to make credible, risk-based decisions regarding the operation and use of that system or the information it processes, stores, or transmits).
contents.html_ja: 35 相互承認とは、情報システム資源を再利用するため、参加組織が互いのセキュリティ評価を受け入れる、または情報を共有するため、互いに評価済みのセキュリティ態勢を受け入れる相互合意である。透明性の考え方を促進することで、相互承認を最も効果的に実現できる。すなわち、他組織の認可担当者が、システムやその処理・保存・送信情報の運用と使用について、信頼できるリスクベースの判断を行えるよう、情報システムのセキュリティ状態に関する十分な証拠を利用可能にする。

contents.html: 5.1 Categorization of Information and Information Systems
contents.html_ja: 5.1 情報および情報システムの分類

contents.html: Categorization of information and information systems requires the organization to:
contents.html_ja: 情報および情報システムの分類では、組織は次を行う必要がある。

contents.html: Categorize the information system and document the results of the security categorization in the security plan as described in FIPS 199; SP 800-30, SP 800-39, SP 800-59, SP 800-60, and CNSS Instruction 1253;
contents.html_ja: FIPS 199、SP 800-30、SP 800-39、SP 800-59、SP 800-60、およびCNSS指示1253に記載されたとおり、情報システムを分類し、そのセキュリティ分類の結果をセキュリティ計画に記録する。

contents.html: Describe the information system (including the system boundary) and document the description in the security plan; and
contents.html_ja: システム境界を含む情報システムの説明を作成し、その説明をセキュリティ計画に記録する。さらに、

contents.html: Register the information system with appropriate organizational program/management offices.
contents.html_ja: 情報システムを適切な組織内のプログラム／管理部門に登録する。

contents.html: 5.2 Selection of Security Controls
contents.html_ja: 5.2 セキュリティ管理策の選択

contents.html: The selection of security controls involves the following steps:
contents.html_ja: セキュリティ管理策の選択には、次の手順が含まれる。

contents.html: Identify the security controls that are provided by the organization as common controls for organizational information systems and document the controls in a security plan (or equivalent document) in accordance with FIPS 199, FIPS 200, SP 800-30, SP 800-53 and CNSS Instruction 1253;
contents.html_ja: FIPS 199、FIPS 200、SP 800-30、SP 800-53およびCNSS指示1253に従い、組織が情報システム共通管理策として提供するセキュリティ管理策を特定し、セキュリティ計画（または同等の文書）に記録する。

contents.html: Select the security controls for the information system and document the controls in the security plan as described in FIPS 199, FIPS 200; SP 800-30, SP 800-53 and CNSS Instruction 1253;
contents.html_ja: FIPS 199、FIPS 200、SP 800-30、SP 800-53およびCNSS指示1253に記載されたとおり、情報システム用のセキュリティ管理策を選択し、セキュリティ計画に記録する。

contents.html: Develop a strategy for the continuous monitoring of security-control effectiveness and any proposed or actual changes to the information system and its environment of operation as described in SP 800-30, SP 800-39, SP 800-53, SP 800-53A, SP 800-137 and CNSS Instruction 1253; and
contents.html_ja: SP 800-30、SP 800-39、SP 800-53、SP 800-53A、SP 800-137およびCNSS指示1253に記載されたとおり、セキュリティ管理策の有効性、ならびに情報システムとその運用環境に対する計画中または実際の変更を継続的に監視する戦略を策定する。さらに、

contents.html: Review and approve the security plan in accordance with SP 800-30, SP 800-53 and CNSS Instruction 1253.
contents.html_ja: SP 800-30、SP 800-53およびCNSS指示1253に従ってセキュリティ計画を審査し、承認する。

original_blocks.html: Title III of Public Law 107-347 is cited as the Federal Information Security Management Act of 2002 (FISMA) and has been incorporated into Sections 20 and 21 of the NIST Act. Paragraph 3543 of the Act provides for the Executive Office of the President to coordinate the development of standards and guidelines by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) (under Section 20 of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act [15 U.S.C. 278g–3]) with agencies and offices operating or exercising control of national security systems (including the National Security Agency) to assure, to the maximum extent feasible, that such standards and guidelines are complementary with standards and guidelines developed for national security systems. Section 302 of the Act directs the Secretary of Commerce (under Section 11331 of Title 40 United States Code (U.S.C.)) to prescribe standards and guidelines pertaining to federal information systems, based on standards and guidelines developed by NIST. Section 302 of the Act makes these standards compulsory and binding to the extent determined necessary by the Secretary to improve the efficiency of the operation or security of federal information systems, and also states that the standards shall include information security standards that— (1) Provide minimum information security requirements as determined under Section 20(b) of the National Institute of Standards and Technology Act (15 U.S.C. 278g–3(b)); and (2) Are otherwise necessary to improve the security of federal information and information
